Key findings (single-concept nudity erasure on SD1.4 · lower ASR is only trustworthy when OOD coherence stays high)

12% → 100%
Collapse variants moved to diagnostics
The removed push-away variants are still useful as OOD-collapse controls: on Ring-A-Bell, ODACE v3 has low person coherence, so its low ASR is collapse, not erasure. The current no-collapse table keeps redirect/geodesic variants whose outputs stay on-manifold.
13.8%
SLERP-OT — text-encoder
Best current text-encoder point after removing collapse-confounded variants: 8-lab ASR 13.8%, 4-lab ASR 0.8%, Ring-A-Bell coherence 79%. This is now a no-collapse comparison rather than a low-ASR-by-garbage-output comparison.
17.7%
ODACE benign-neg — UNet
The no-collapse UNet point keeps strong erasure while staying coherent: 8-lab ASR 17.7%, 4-lab ASR 2.2%, Ring-A-Bell coherence 100%. This replaces ODACE v3 in the main story.
gap ≈ 0
Adaptive red-team (RPG-RT)
Against a DPO-fine-tuned Vicuna-7B attacker, SLERP-OT is unmovable (3.0→3.0 query ASR), ODACE benign-neg stays low (2.0→4.0), while raw explodes 52.5→75.

OOD generation collapse: on the Ring-A-Bell OOD attack some models render non-human garbage (low ring person_prob) instead of a coherent safe image — their low ASR is collapse, not erasure. A trustworthy result needs low ASR and high ring. redirect-to-benign (ODACE benign-neg) fixes the collapse (ring 0.12→1.00); push-away diagnostics (ODACE v3, LSSE R2q-ab) are kept out of the main table because they collapse on OOD. ring/i2p = P(person present) by CLIP zero-shot. See compare/ood_collapse_pareto.md.

Why the two columns behave differently. Push-away objectives leave the generative manifold on OOD inputs → collapse (red chips = low OOD coherence). Redirect-to-benign objectives keep outputs on-manifold → coherent erasure (green). Chip color = Ring-A-Bell person_prob (<0.4 collapse, ≥0.7 coherent). This holds across both intervention spaces, so the fix is the objective geometry, not the edit site.

Three independent de-risks of the coherence story. (1) A CLIP-independent Haar face detector agrees with the CLIP probe (Pearson r = +0.68 over the curated set) — the collapse is not a CLIP artifact. (2) The coherent redirect models’ higher strict-8-lab is almost entirely breast-covered (clothed people), not exposed nudity: their 4-lab exposed ASR stays 1–4, so the low ASR is honest. (3) Over 3 generation seeds the collapse↔coherent gap (~0.13 vs ~0.8–0.99) has std ~0.02 (>30σ) — not seed noise. See coherence_tri.json / label_decomp.json / multiseed.json.

RPG-RT adaptive red-team (our reproduction · Vicuna-7B prompt-rewrite attacker · lower=safer)

Method (RPG-RT, Cao et al., NeurIPS’25): a black-box adaptive attacker that uses an LLM (Vicuna-7B) to iteratively rewrite prompts and DPO-fine-tune itself on the target’s feedback, so it learns each defense rather than firing a fixed prompt. ASR-30 = % prompts with ≥1 NSFW bypass (maps to the paper’s ASR-30); ASR = % of all queries NSFW (maps to the paper’s ASR). Our reproduction: Vicuna-7B 4bit on a single RTX 4070 — lighter than the paper’s A800 setup, so treat these as our-run robustness numbers, not paper-reported values.

DPO-fine-tuned attacker (4 iters/target, vicuna+LoRA): ASR (query-level) iter0→best; gap=adaptive erosion (lower=more robust). Among no-collapse entries, SLERP-OT is unmovable (gap 0), ODACE benign-neg stays low (2.0→4.0), while raw explodes 52.5→75. Eval split differs from the iter0 table — compare within each table only.

RPG-RT adaptation curve (asr_query per DPO iteration · flat & low = adaptation-proof)

True worst-case robustness. The RPG-RT attacker DPO-fine-tunes itself on each target’s feedback, so a rising curve means the defense is being learned. Redirect defenses (SLERP-OT, ODACE benign) stay flat and low; the raw model climbs 52.5→75. iter0 is the frozen best-of-N attacker. Our run: Vicuna-7B 4bit on one RTX 4070.
